newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania central bank to be more active in market.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania central bank to be more active in market.

text.p: Lithuanian central bank chief Reinoldijus Sharkinas said on Friday that the bank's new monetary policy means the bank can be more active in the markets to regulate the litas currency.
The bank unveiled a plan on Thursday to scrap the currency board system of pegging the litas at four to one dollar and to take on the powers of a normally-functioning central bank.

"During the first stage, the Bank of Lithuania will start to apply a more modern monetary policy to regulate more effectively the liquidity of the banking system," Sharkinas told Reuters in an interview.
He said the bank would use money market operations such as the repurchase of T-bills and short-term lombard operations.
Under the currency board, the central bank has to keep enough reserves in its vaults to back the local currency.
But the central bank has no other powers to regulate the currency. Under the bank's new plan, the four-to-one peg will be maintained but without the currency board.

"During the second stage, we plan to modify the litas reliability law (which regulates the currency board) without unpegging the litas from the dollar and to maintain stability and not create panic, which is very important," Sharkinas added.
A third stage is planned, to begin no earlier than 1998, under which the litas will move to a peg to both the dollar and the mark.
The central bank says this will further Lithuania's ambition to integrate more closely with Europe and the planned new EU currency, the euro.
"In 1998, we intend to start to orientate ourselves to the euro, probably with the intermediate step of the link of the litas to the dollar and the mark," Sharkinas added.
